gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's own RV5 page tells RVs with 12V auto-leveling systems that draw more than 100 A at startup to add a separate 12V battery (BLUETTI B1210 at $299, or keep the existing 12V lead-acid battery). The $4,299 5kWh RV Kit + 4 × 100W does not include that battery.
standout_why: Victron's sizing article (cited) covers partial shading, cable size, combined Voc, fuses, the PV isolator and Victron controller details. It never mentions leveling jacks or slide-outs, a separate 12V battery next to a higher-voltage system, or the open-ground/floating-neutral problem. smartrvhub (top result) covers 12V vs 24V and DC-DC alternator charging. It never mentions 48V systems feeding 12V loads, leveling jacks, floating neutral or lithium cold charging. I couldn't compare Renogy's guide (cited) properly: WebFetch got only 6,868 characters of navigation and no article text, and my curl fallback was not approved. The finding decides the set because it adds a line item (the B1210) to the cart, and none of the pages I could read mention it.
kit_items: Power hub + 48V battery + panels: BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 4 × 100W (RV5 hub, B4810 51.2 V 100 Ah, Epanel, Epad, 4 × 100 W). It is BLUETTI's own one-SKU RV solar kit, and the store page lists battery, alternator-charger and distribution-panel wiring packs in the box.

12V buffer battery: BLUETTI B1210 12.8 V 100 Ah LiFePO4. BLUETTI's RV5 page names it for 12V auto-leveling systems with startup currents over 100 A. The store page says it has self-heating below 0 °C (32 °F).
Panel wiring: parallel, not series. Backup Power Hub lists the RV5 PV1 input at 50 V max and says panels must be wired in parallel.

findings.label: Maker's instruction for 12V auto-leveling loads
findings.value: For 12V auto-leveling systems with startup currents over 100 A, pair with a dedicated B1210 battery or the vehicle's existing 12V lead-acid battery
findings.note: Quoted from the maker's US product page. The same sentence is on the 5kWh RV Kit + 4 × 100W page (https://www.bluettipower.com/products/rv5-b4810-epanel-epad-2-200w). Neither page's box list includes a 12V battery.

findings.label: DC output
findings.value: 1,620 W DC output, rated 12 V/24 V
findings.note: The maker gives DC output in watts only, not amps.

findings.label: 12V DC converter output current
findings.source_title: Bluetti RV5 Review: 5,000W RV Solar System (2026), Andrew Harrington, Backup Power Hub
findings.note: From Andrew Harrington's spec table. The article was first published 2026-04-07 and updated 2026-09-27. The 100 A figure matches BLUETTI's own 100 A startup threshold for leveling systems.

findings.label: Solar input limit (PV1)
findings.value: 1,800 W max, 50 V max. Panels must be wired in parallel, not in series
findings.source_title: Bluetti RV5 Review: 5,000W RV Solar System (2026), Andrew Harrington, Backup Power Hub
findings.note: This is the reviewer's figure. BLUETTI's own RV5 page does not state a PV voltage limit. The same review says PV2 also serves as the alternator input (1,200 W at 24 V, 600 W at 12 V), so it can't take a second solar array, and that output derates above 6,561 ft (2,000 m).

findings.label: Price today

findings.label: Price and cold-weather charging
findings.value: $299.00. 12.8 V 100 Ah. Self-heating film turns on below 0 °C (32 °F) and keeps the cells around 25 °C (77 °F)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI B1210 LiFePO4 Battery | 12.8 V, 100 Ah (bluettipower.com)
findings.note: The page also shows a Black Friday Early Access offer (Nov 5–18), so prices may change. It does not state max continuous or surge discharge current. The same page lists the B4810 at $1,699.

findings.product: general (portable power station feeding an RV shore inlet)
findings.label: Floating neutral trips the RV's surge protector/EMS
findings.value: Power stations have no ground bond, so a Progressive EMS reads 'open ground' and won't pass power to the RV. Fix: a neutral-ground bonding plug in a 3-way adapter on the power station
findings.source_title: Solar Generator N-G Bonding?, Mike Sokol, RVelectricity, 2023-01-20
findings.note: One reader report: the reader's ALLPOWERS unit was flagged by their Progressive device. Sokol names Jackery, Bluetti, Goal Zero and ALLPOWERS as makers of these 'solar generators'. This applies to the power-station route (e.g. the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 or ALLPOWERS kits Dealectric lists), not to the hard-wired RV5.
